_comment: Curated third-party skills. Deliberately small. Every skill's name and description sits in context every session, and overlapping descriptions cause the wrong skill to grab a turn - so ten good skills beat fifty. Entries are pinned to a commit SHA, never a branch: a moving upstream is unreviewed code running on user machines.
bar: Does it earn its permanent context cost, or is it a one-off you could just ask for?
Is it prose, or does it ship executable code? Code must be read line by line before vendoring.
Does its license permit redistribution, and have we carried the attribution files?
Does it conflict with easyClaude's own workflow, cost posture, or SessionStart hook?
Does it duplicate something already shipped, here or by Anthropic?

vendored.name: slopmonster
vendored.why: The only mechanical check here aimed at prose rather than code. verify.mjs decides whether the build is honest; nothing decided whether the words were, and "make it sound less like a robot" was a judgement call every time. This makes it falsifiable: five rule groups, one point each, exits non-zero below 5/5, and every rule can be looked up and argued with. It is built in by request, not by the bar - see _vendored_comment.
vendored.reviewed: Both executable files were read in full before vendoring, per the bar. tools/deslop.py imports re, sys and html, opens files only to read them, and makes no network call, no subprocess call and no eval. tools/cleanse.sh pipes the draft to whichever rival model CLI is installed (codex exec, or claude -p), which means the draft leaves the machine and the call is billed. That is the step's whole purpose and it is documented, not hidden. Full notes in skills/slopmonster/PROVENANCE.md.
vendored.needs: Python 3 for the linter; bash and awk for the cleanse step. This is the first runtime dependency outside Node that this plugin has ever carried, and it is the reason to re-read that trade if it ever grows a second one. On Windows the command is python, not python3.

_vendored_comment: Carries one skill, by explicit request rather than by the bar above. slopmonster is not prose-only, it needs a runtime this plugin otherwise does not use, and one of its two scripts sends your draft to a second model provider and bills you for it. Every one of those is a reason the bar would normally refuse. They are written down in the entry and in PROVENANCE.md instead of being smoothed over, because the point of a bar is that going around it leaves a record. design-taste sat here until 2026-09-19 and was removed for the opposite reason: it picked an aesthetic for everybody. A slop linter is a checker rather than a taste, which is the line being drawn - you can disagree with one of its five rules and go read it.
_catalogue_comment: The recommendations the user actually sees live in reference/skills-catalogue.md, not here, and they cover security, testing, marketing and document work as well as design. That file is a catalogue, not a registry, and the bar above does not apply to it: nothing in it is vendored, pinned, or shipped, so nothing in it runs on a user machine unless that user installs it themselves. What applies instead is one rule borrowed from scripts/connect.mjs - every entry was checked against the GitHub API before it was written down, because a catalogue that 404s on first use is worse than no catalogue. Recheck the counts and licences when you touch it; they drift.

recommended_not_vendored.name: hallmark
recommended_not_vendored.author: Nutlope (Hassan El Mghari)
recommended_not_vendored.verdict: Offered by /easyclaude:skills as the light design pick, and described in full in reference/skills-catalogue.md. Prose only, MIT, no hooks, no binaries, nothing to approve. Pick it unless you specifically want impeccable's browser loop.
why_not_vendored: Choosing between it and impeccable is a taste decision about a project, not a decision this plugin should make once for everybody.
Vendoring both would put two design descriptions in every turn's context, and they describe nearly the same job - which is the wrong-skill-grabs-the-turn failure check 9 warns about.

Its SKILL.md is 66KB, roughly 16k tokens whenever it fires. Installed in the user's own project that cost is visible to them; vendored here it would hide behind a budget gate that measures descriptions, not bodies.

recommended_not_vendored.name: impeccable
recommended_not_vendored.author: Paul Bakaus; derives in part from Anthropic's frontend-design skill
recommended_not_vendored.verdict: Offered by /easyclaude:skills as the heavy design pick, and described in full in reference/skills-catalogue.md. It drives a real browser, screenshots its own output and critiques it, which is a genuinely different loop. It also installs hooks and runs a downloaded binary, so it is a deliberate choice, not a default.
why_not_vendored: It ships executable code: launcher scripts, a JS browser bundle, and an engine binary that downloads on first run into ~/.impeccable/bin/. The bar above says code is read line by line before vendoring, and a binary fetched at run time cannot be read at all.

Its installer writes provider-native hooks into .claude/settings.local.json. Upstream's own README warns those run independently of model-tool approval, so a first edit can fetch and cache the engine even in a session that denied the command.

Those hooks land on the same events hooks/hooks.json already owns. This is the graft init argument again: the good part is worth having, the installer is not something to run for someone without saying so.

recommended_not_vendored.name: task-observer
recommended_not_vendored.aka: One Skill to Rule Them All
recommended_not_vendored.author: Eoghan Henn / rebelytics.com
recommended_not_vendored.verdict: Genuinely good and actively maintained. Install it alongside easyClaude if you want it - but knowingly, not by default.
why_not_vendored: Its own instructions require invocation before the first tool call of every session and before any plan is written. easyClaude's SessionStart hook already owns the session opener and plan-feature owns planning, so the two would compete for the same moments.
Its SKILL.md is 44KB - roughly 11k tokens whenever it triggers, against a framework measured at ~1.4k tokens/turn that ships .mcp.json empty specifically to avoid this kind of cost.
It needs a persistent workspace at a stable absolute path and ships two Python scripts, against easyClaude's zero-runtime-dependency design.
It is a peer framework, not a component. Bundling it would silently make easyClaude a different product.

_budget_comment: Everything loaded on EVERY turn of EVERY session: rules/*.md, the name and description of each skill that does not set disable-model-invocation, and the name, description and tool list of each agent in agents/. An agent has no equivalent of disable-model-invocation: it is listed on every turn or it does not ship, which is why one ships and the bar for a second is the same bar as a vendored skill. Occasional skills set that flag, cost nothing until invoked as /easyclaude:<name>, and stay discoverable via one pointer line in rules/workflow.md. CI fails if the total exceeds max_always_on_tokens. Commands are not counted because Claude Code does not load them until they are typed, which is why /easyclaude:skills and the catalogue it reads can afford to be as long as they need to be. An entry there costs a user nothing until they install it - and costs them on every turn once they do, which is the arithmetic the catalogue leads with.
_budget_headroom_comment: Raised from 1200 to 1400 on purpose. At 1200 the measured figure sat 28 tokens under the cap, which is not a budget - it is a tripwire on the next sentence anyone writes. A cap that fails on an ordinary edit gets raised in the same commit as the edit, by whoever is annoyed, without the trade being looked at. 1400 leaves room for roughly one more always-on skill and no more, so the next raise is still a decision someone has to argue for. Spend it on a skill that has to hear plain English; anything that can be typed as /easyclaude:<name> sets disable-model-invocation and costs nothing. Removing vendored design-taste on 2026-09-19 gave back 156 of those tokens; the cap stays where it is, because headroom that gets spent the moment it appears was never a budget either.
